subject: Spike in errors and reserved throughput gap — urgent cross-team coordination (BoltBank)
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@boltbank.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency/error spike affecting live payments flows

Hi Tessa / Marissa / Marcus,

We're seeing a significant increase in tail latency and a rising 5xx rate from the Redwood Dedicated pool that services our reserved capacity. The last two hours show sustained latency > 1.8s p95 (normally ~400ms) and several failed payment attempts. Our ops team is holding traffic but we need remediation and an ETA. This is impacting customer checkout and will hit our SLAs.

Action requested: can Redwood confirm whether this is a reserved-capacity degradation vs. a model-level issue? We need an ETA for mitigation and a short note we can send to internal stakeholders. Procurement is already pinging us about credits.

I've attached our monitoring snapshot for the last 3 hours.

Attachments: boltbank-screens-1625.png (screenshot), error-log-tail.txt

Thanks,
Sarah Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
BoltBank
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Thanks Sarah — looping in infra/SRE. Marcus / Karthik, can you triage and confirm whether this is pool saturation, queued requests spiking, or a model-execution regression? Please post quick findings and any proposed mitigations (temporary and medium-term).

Marissa / Evelyn, heads-up for CS and account engagement — Sarah flagged procurement asking about credits. If this is a capacity shortfall on our side we'll need a customer-facing note and an ask for leadership engagement.

Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency/error spike affecting live payments flows

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed: sustained worker queue depth increase on Dedicated pool D-P-3 servicing BoltBank's reserved capacity. KV-cache hit ratios stable.
- Error profile: bursts of 503/504 from inference runtime when queue length > 1100 (threshold is 800 on this fleet).
- Hypothesis: rapid background surge from a small set of high-TPS flows + autoscaler not reacting due to config limits on reserved pool.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (rolling):
1) Temporarily raise reserved pool headroom for BoltBank (manual uplift to add 2 GPU cards to D-P-3) — ETA 30m if approved.
2) Enable degraded-model fallback (switch customers to lower-latency quantized variant) — ETA 20m but will reduce generation quality slightly.
3) Apply short-term request throttling with graceful 429s and retry-after headers to reduce queue pressure — ETA 10m (requires prod-ratelimit change).

I've uploaded a snapshot of traces and queue metrics (queue_metrics_q2.csv, slo-trace-snapshot.png). Will continue collecting logs.

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency/error spike affecting live payments flows

Customer update draft (for review):
- What happened: We experienced an unexpected surge in requests that caused temporary queueing and elevated error rates for a subset of traffic on your reserved capacity.
- Impact: Some payment attempts returned errors or were delayed; we've isolated affected windows and are working on immediate mitigations.
- Next steps: We will (1) add capacity to the reserved pool, (2) enable a temporary fallback to the quantized model to reduce latency while preserving throughput, and (3) offer a credit for the impacted period.

Evelyn / Tessa — do we need exec-level approval for the credit? If so, Jonas should weigh in (I can scope the proposed credit % once we know the exact downtime window).

Attachments: customer-runbook.pdf (internal runbook excerpt)

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 18:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in errors and reserved throughput gap — urgent cross-team coordination (BoltBank)

Thanks for the triage summary and for fast-moving mitigations. Quick notes / asks for closure before I loop in the executive bridge:
1) Confirmed actions taken: uplifted 2 GPUs to D-P-3 at 16:18 PDT on 2027-05-16; quantized fallback enabled at 16:40 PDT; short-term throttling applied at 16:50 PDT. Can we capture the precise window of customer impact (start/end) and the observed error delta? Marcus, please paste the 5xx count and p95 before/after in the thread.
2) Compensation: Marissa — propose offering a 10% service credit on the impacted invoice if the impact window exceeds 45 minutes. If under 45m, offer 5%. Please run this by finance (cc: we didn't include finance yet).
3) Root cause follow-up: Karthik — prioritize a post-mortem to identify why autoscaler failed to add headroom for reserved pool and whether the routing policy caused cross-customer contention. Root cause + remediation plan due EOD Friday.
4) Exec bridge: I'll prepare a one-slide summary for leadership and the account exec. Tessa — can you draft a 2-3 line note for the CEO-facing summary we can use if BoltBank escalates?

I'll be on call tomorrow morning; if we need fast exec attention I'll pull the bridge. Good work triaging — let's close the loop with clear timelines so CS can re-engage the customer.

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Reliability
